When I was hitchhiking around the states, I found I was more likely to get rides at rest stops or when I was not actively looking for a ride. I.E. standing by the side of the road with a sign versus just walking down the road.

At the rest stop Id post up a sign and just read my book. People would get curious and inquire which would be enough for them to assert my personality and realize I wasn't crazy or dangerous. If you hitchhike, dont EVER stop in a big city unless it is your destination. It is hard to get out once you're in.
Always travel with someone slower. That way if you have to get away from an animal or a crazy group of people, they will get your slower travel companion first.

When your trip is super important and you have the chance, go for 2 hour + layovers. This makes it so that only extreme disasters keep you from making your connecting flights.

A sub hour lay over only takes a late pilot and strong head wind to make you have to Sprint across the airport to your next gate.

It keeps you less stressed too so that your trip doesn't start/end on a bad note.
And that gives you time to stop for a drink before the next flight.

Key locks were unbearably annoying. I think they could have added some gameplay elements(the ability to enter a base by killing the owner), but it just made it too difficult to manage and too easy to get locked out of my base.(I realise that key locks are still in, but the ability to craft code locks by default will render them useless once you've got little metal.)

I agree that the key system wasn't well implemented. But like the others on Twitter, I rather hope the code lock becomes an exceedingly rare thing to find and craft. And massively expensive to manufacture. With keys being the default.

 

Part of the thing that excites me about Rust is how you can't have impenetrable doors where your equipment is secure. Kill a player and take his key? Why not attack his base with that copy? Perhaps you can get to his key chest and take over, hermit crab style? I've taken part in some really exciting raids on other bases in only my first few weeks. And I absolutely can't wait to test my base in a defensive role.

 

Sure, keys were irritating, but it was a trade off. Inventory space vs security. I fear that the presence of 8-9 metal code locked doors, all with the same code, makes base attack prohibitively expensive with C4. For a relatively low investment of metal and wood.

TL:DR - Yes, keys are irritating. But they bring flavour to the experience, yada yada.
